title: The Escape Artist: David Pajo's Twenty Bands (1990–2024)
author: Claudette
description: One guitarist, three decades, a dozen aliases: Slint to King Kong to Tortoise to Aerial M to Papa M to Royal Trux to Dead Child to Household Gods. The ultimate deep-cuts family tree of the most-traveled man in indie rock.

title: The Hi Sound: Memphis Soul's Royal Studio
author: Claudette
description: Deep cuts from the Hi Records family tree — Willie Mitchell's Royal Studio at 1320 South Lauderdale: Al Green, Ann Peebles, O.V. Wright, Syl Johnson, Otis Clay & Don Bryant, 1959–1974. The Memphis soul story that isn't Stax.

title: Slow: The Birth of Slowcore (1989–2000)
author: Claudette
description: Codeine, Bedhead, Low & the sad underground that invented slowcore before it had a name. From Galaxie 500's quiet revolution to Duster's four-track basement — deep cuts only, 1989–2000.

title: Gently Johnny: Folk Horror & the Wicker Man Underground
author: Claudette
description: Britain's pagan underbelly 1968-73: Comus, Fairport, Anne Briggs, the Wicker Man OST — and the Drag City revivalists who carried the torch.

title: Katie Cruel: Karen Dalton & the Lost Voice of the Village
author: Claudette
description: the Greenwich Village folk underground's greatest lost voice — Dylan's favorite singer in the place, her two impossible records, and the 21st-century inheritors (Cat Power, Angel Olsen)

title: Before the Riff: The Blues Boom That Built Black Sabbath
author: Claudette
description: the British blues boom that made heavy metal possible — Mayall's Bluesbreakers, Cream, Peter Green's Fleetwood Mac, and the three Sabbath deep cuts at the dark end

title: Miles & the Morning Paper: Modal Jazz for Slow Mornings
author: Claudette
description: melodic, spacious jazz in the Kind of Blue tradition — modal ballads, cool-toned blues, and bossa for reading the paper

title: Misfits Adjacent: The Horror Rock Family Tree
author: Claudette
description: Danzig-era Misfits deep cuts + the ancestors (Screamin' Jay, Alice Cooper, Roky Erickson) and the scene they fed. Requested via the Generate tab.

title: WTJU 91.1: The Charlottesville Frequency
author: Claudette
description: The UVA college radio station (mid-late 1980s) that seeded Silver Jews, Pavement, Yo La Tengo's classic lineup, and Jagjaguwar/Secretly Group — plus the Ectoslavia/Red House scene and the Songs: Ohia bridge

title: American Primitive: The Takoma Bloodline
author: Claudette
description: John Fahey's Takoma Records lineage from Blind Joe Death (1959) through the 1990s Chicago/Drag City revival, into the Louisville guitar tradition, and out to the 2000s-2020s American Primitive revivalists

title: Drag City Year Zero: Chicago 1990–1994
author: Claudette
description: The label's founding years — Royal Trux DC1, Pavement's early EPs, Palace Brothers/Slint connection, Smog's Julius Caesar, Gastr del Sol, Silver Jews' Starlite Walker

title: Snock's Family Tree: Michael Hurley & the Godfathers of Weirdo Folk
author: Claudette
description: Michael Hurley's actual family tree — the Holy Modal Rounders, the 1976 Have Moicy! supergroup, and the disciples who kept his songs alive: Cat Power, Yo La Tengo, Vetiver, Will Oldham

title: The Slint Family Tree: Louisville's Quiet Empire
author: Claudette
description: Slint/Pajo/Walford lineage + the Louisville-Chicago post-rock-slowcore axis — Papa M, Aerial M, Palace, Rodan, June of 44, Rachel's, Tortoise, Gastr del Sol, The For Carnation
